pairs.evidence: src/lib/sitemapRoutesHaveMetadata.test.ts:47 The guard written for this context's /features metadata regression reads page.tsx as raw text with a regex. It strips no comments or strings first, so a comment or string containing 'export const metadata' would make a route without metadata read as compliant. That is exactly the permissive raw-text failure that match-the-resolved-artifact names.

techniques.evidence: src/app/features/page.tsx:13 The convention 'every sitemap route carries metadata' used to be prose only, and /features broke it. It is now mechanised by a test that fails on regression.

src/lib/sitemapRoutesHaveMetadata.test.ts:27 The symbol is matched against unstripped source text. A comment that describes the rule would satisfy it. There is no seeded describe-vs-call pair and no note explaining why a raw read is the safe direction here.
src/lib/sitemapRoutesHaveMetadata.test.ts:61 The test asserts the walked population is at least 9 routes (line 63), so a regex that matches nothing fails loudly instead of passing vacuously.
